schema.description: A specialty coffee roastery that buys beans from farms around the world, roasts them in batches, supplies its own cafés, and has its baristas taste and score every coffee.

knot.description: Country where coffee is grown, such as Ethiopia, Colombia, Kenya or Guatemala.
How the coffee cherry is removed from the bean after harvest, such as washed, natural, honey or anaerobic. Strongly affects flavor.
How far a batch is roasted: light, medium or dark.
A flavor note from the coffee flavor wheel, such as blueberry, jasmine, dark chocolate, caramel or citrus.
Way a coffee is prepared and served, such as espresso, filter, pour-over or cold brew.

anchor.description: A coffee farm or washing station that the roastery buys green beans from.

attribute.description: Country where the farm is located.
Altitude of the farm in meters above sea level. Higher altitudes usually give denser beans with more acidity.

anchor.description: A lot of green coffee beans bought from a farm, sold under its own name.

attribute.description: Name the coffee is sold under, such as Yirgacheffe Kochere.
Botanical variety of the coffee plant, such as Geisha, Bourbon, Typica or SL28.
Processing method used for this lot.
Price paid per kilogram of green beans, in euros. Historized, since prices change with every harvest and contract.

anchor.description: A café run by the roastery, where its coffee is brewed and served.

attribute.description: Name of the café. Historized, since cafés are sometimes rebranded.
City where the café is located.
Number of seats in the café. Historized, since it changes with renovations and outdoor seating seasons.

anchor.description: A barista who brews coffee in the cafés and takes part in cuppings.

attribute.description: The drink the barista is currently known for. Historized, since every barista reinvents it now and then.

nexus.description: A single roast batch, in which one bean is roasted to a chosen level.

attribute.description: Date and time when the batch was roasted.
Weight of the roasted batch in kilograms.
Length of the roast in seconds, from charging the drum to dropping the beans.

role.description: The level the batch was roasted to.

nexus.description: A cupping, a standardized tasting in which a barista scores a coffee and notes its most striking flavor.

attribute.description: Date and time of the cupping.
Cupping score on the specialty coffee scale from 0 to 100, where 80 or more counts as specialty coffee.

role.description: The barista who did the tasting.
The dominant flavor note found in the cup.

tie.description: The farm a bean was grown at. Every bean comes from exactly one farm, while a farm can supply many beans.

role.description: The farm where the bean was grown.

tie.description: The menu of each café: which beans it serves, and prepared in which ways. Historized, since menus rotate with the seasons.
The café where a barista works. A barista works at one café at a time, but may move between cafés over time.

role.description: The café the barista works at.

tie.description: Who trained whom. Every barista is trained by one more experienced barista, who may train many.

role.description: The barista who did the training.

tie.description: Deliveries of roast batches to cafés. A batch can be split between several cafés.

role.description: The roast batch that was delivered.
The café that received the delivery.
